label: digit 1 fed back as input during copy phase
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, when the input token is the digit 1 (the model just output 1 and fed it back), from recall_idx >= 2 on. It never fires on 1 during the original phase, at the delimiter, or on any other token; it is mostly silent on 1 at recall_idx 1, which holds the remaining few percent of activations (all low). Magnitude: in examples, activations are lowest when the 1 sits early in the sequence (about 0.5-0.7 of max) and highest when it sits further in (about 0.95+). Within a run of repeated 1s, the second 1 fires a little weaker (about 0.8) than the first. Out_tok, prev_tok and L have little effect.

issues: No systematic counterexample found. Test split: 0 false positives. All 1574 missed activations (0.1% of mass) are 1 fed back at recall_idx 1, i.e. the first copied token. These are all very weak (0.01-0.04 of max), which matches the explanation's 'mostly silent on 1 at recall_idx 1'.
Phase claims hold. The profile shows 0 activations in the original and delimiter phases. in_tok=1 carries 100% of activation mass, apart from one stray activation on 'l'.
Widening to recall_idx >= 1 gives recall 1.0 but precision 0.834 (test F1 0.909), so the recall_idx >= 2 cutoff is justified.

Minor: the specific magnitude figures (0.5-0.7 vs 0.95+, ~0.8 for a repeated 1) were not checked with targeted predicates. They are descriptive and do not affect the predicate. Correlation of the predicate with activation is 0.99.
